whys.why: Why does git-port.test.ts hold names off the casing convention?
whys.because: It writes out the environment keys the git port strips or keeps.

whys.why: Why does the test write out the environment keys the git port strips or keeps?
whys.because: The git port decides which environment keys reach the git subprocess.

whys.why: Why does the git port decide which environment keys reach the git subprocess?
whys.because: Git reads GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE from its environment and would act on another repository.

whys.why: Why does git read GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE from its environment?
whys.because: Git's contract names those environment variables, and POSIX names PATH and HOME.

whys.why: Why are those environment variable names in that casing?
whys.because: Git and POSIX define the environment variable names outside our code.

whyChain.rootCause: Git and POSIX define the environment variable names outside our code.
